analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes: docs/developer/test.md (head text at lines 1843-2555, which includes the changed ranges 1878-1883 and 2229-2246 plus unchanged surrounding test descriptions) and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (a date bump at line 3 and a new Gemma 4 pipeline lanes sentence at lines 159-161). No code, protocol, key-handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage logic is changed.

Security-relevant context checked:
- The test.md prose on the cluster prefix tenant partition (around lines 2175-2196) and the SSD prefix record encoding (around lines 2320-2369) remains consistent with T-041. It describes tenant-partitioned prefix caches and says tenant isolation on a real model and pair is still a hardware gate. It makes no claim that would weaken the SEC-035 accepted risk, and it extends no TTL or scope.
- The wording on Gemma pipeline lanes, installed batch-lane propagation and the Gemma routed-expert prior only describes concurrency and lane-default behavior (serial-prefill pipeline takes multiple lanes, one-chunk lookahead keeps one). That is availability and performance configuration. It is documented as unqualified on hardware, with no new trust boundary.
- The docs explicitly disclaim qualification, and no new endpoint, key custody or secret is introduced.

Remaining questions for integration: the claimed behavior (DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes reaching the rank, and multi-lane Gemma pipeline concurrency) lives in code outside this batch. Whether that code correctly preserves per-request prefix-cache partitioning and memory admission under multi-lane Gemma serving cannot be verified from these docs. Any code change in the PR that enables default multi-lane Gemma pipeline serving should be checked against T-041 (cache salt and tenant isolation across lanes) and against availability and memory-admission limits. No finding is raised from the documentation alone.
